topic: The chainsaw was invented to help in difficult childbirth (Aitken & Jeffray, 1780s)
taste: No patient, no body, no blood, no operation shown. Only the two doctors, a clock, and the tool on a blueprint. Friendly cartoon.

claims.claim: Scottish doctors John Aitken and James Jeffray are credited with the first chain saw, in the 1780s.
It was made for difficult childbirth: a procedure that needed bone cut, which was slow by knife.
It was a fine chain with serrated teeth, pulled back and forth by two handles.
Later versions were fitted with a hand crank.
In 1905 San Francisco logger Samuel Bens patented an 'endless chain saw' meant for giant redwoods.
